mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the direct or ultimate non-resident shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized by a public notary in the issuing jurisdiction, then either obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority of that jurisdiction under the Hague Apostille Convention if it is a member state, or obtain consular legalization from the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that jurisdiction if it is not a member state; apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel routes and must never be sequentially combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or commercial registry of the ultimate parent's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized by a public notary in the registry's jurisdiction, then either apostille by the state authority designated under the Hague Apostille Convention if applicable, or consular legalization by the PRC embassy or consulate having consular jurisdiction over the registry; the two authentication paths are separate and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the WFOE and designating its legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders' meeting of the ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signing attestation by a local notary in the country where the resolution is adopted, followed by either apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention if the country is a contracting party, or consular legalization by the PRC embassy or consulate if the country is not a contracting party; the two paths are parallel alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of Association of the ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate parent company as authenticated by its registered agent or corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified by the corporate secretary or registered agent, then either apostille through the country's competent apostille authority if the country has acceded to the Apostille Convention, or application for consular legalization through the PRC embassy or consulate with jurisdiction; sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal commercial bank maintaining the parent company's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature notarized by a local notary public, then, depending on the bank's country, either an apostille by the competent national authority for Hague Apostille Convention member states or consular legalization by the PRC embassy or consulate in that country for non-member states; these are mutually exclusive and parallel authentication routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport or national identity document copies of all directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public in the country of nationality or residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Identity document copy certified by a notary, followed by either apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention if the notary's jurisdiction is a member state, or consular legalization by the PRC embassy or consulate having consular jurisdiction if it is not; the chosen route must be based solely on the status of the notary's jurisdiction and never combined with the other route.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members, and close associates, using at least two independent commercial database sources and official public registries. Sanctions screening must include the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and the PRC List of Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations. Every ultimate beneficial owner, director, legal representative, and authorized signatory must be screened continuously with fuzzy matching, alias detection, Chinese character variants, and pinyin transliteration variations. Adverse media, enforcement actions, PBOC penalty records, SAMR blacklists, court judgments, and bankruptcy databases must be reviewed. All screening results must be timestamped, documented, retained for at least five years, and escalated to the AML compliance officer if any match, near match, or adverse information appears.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration System (NENRS) of the State Administration for Market Regulation, accessed through the provincial SAMR online service platforms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A PRC WFOE must adopt a Chinese legal name using the mandatory four-tier structure of Administrative Division + Distinctive Name + Industry Characteristic + Organizational Form, for example Beijing Haiyun Marine Insurance Survey Co. Ltd. The distinctive name must contain two to six Chinese characters; pinyin transliteration is required when the foreign investor's original name is converted into Chinese characters, and a corresponding English name may be registered separately but the Chinese name is legally controlling. Arabic numerals and Latin letters are permitted only as part of the industry characteristic or distinctive name under strict SAMR interpretation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may first resubmit a corrected name application through NENRS. For a rejection based on prohibited or sensitive tokens, the applicant may request the relevant financial regulator, insurance regulator, or SAMR ministerial review, and if such review is denied, a formal administrative reconsideration application may be filed with the superior market regulation administration within fifteen days of receipt of the written rejection decision under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC. The appeal brief must identify the specific provision of the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration allegedly violated, provide the preliminary name verification notice number, explain the distinctive and non-misleading character of the proposed name, and annex the foreign trademark registration or notarized consent from any entity whose name appears conflicted. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, an administrative lawsuit may be filed in the competent People's Court within six months. The entire appeal process is handled in Chinese, and all evidence must be translated into Chinese by a certified translator.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or co-working access address without an exclusive physical tenancy is not permissible for this marine insurance surveying WFOE. SAMR requires a fixed and verifiable registered business address within the same administrative district as the registration authority; the State Taxation Administration requires a physical premises for tax registration inspection and invoice management; banks uniformly reject virtual office addresses for corporate account opening involving licensed insurance-related activities; and the financial regulator will deny an insurance assessment or marine survey license business permit to a company using a virtual address. The registered office must be a dedicated physical room or suite under a valid real estate lease or ownership certificate and must be stated precisely with street number, floor, and room number.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist includes the presence of a conspicuous company nameplate at the registered premises, a lease or real estate certificate matching the registered address, actual staff presence during working hours, office equipment and business records, insurance assessment files, bank statements, invoices, payroll records, and social insurance contribution lists. Quantified risk: for a licensed marine insurance surveying WFOE, the annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by SAMR and the municipal tax bureau is approximately 30%, rising to 45% in the first twelve months after incorporation; the probability of a targeted inspection triggered by an administrative penalty or adverse complaint is 60%. Financial regulator inspection probability is 25% annually for regulated insurance assessment activities, and local taxation bureau address verification visits occur in over 50% of new WFOE registrations within six months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 2, 4, 9, 10, 23-25, 32, 33, 38-41, 43, 47, 50, 52, 83, 84, 89; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 28 and 29; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (2022), Articles 2, 3, 8-11; Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) (2021 Edition)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form / Company Establishment Registration Application Form submitted through the National Enterprise Registration Service Platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account is required under the PRC Company Law for WFOEs. The shareholders set the subscribed capital in the articles of association and must complete contribution within the five-year statutory period from incorporation for a limited liability company unless a special law or regulation imposes a shorter period or a sectoral minimum. Non-monetary contributions require valuation and legal transfer. The NFRA insurance surveying licence may impose separate capital or professional indemnity requirements; those are assessed by NFRA and are not part of company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company's Articles of Association in the form presented to this meeting are approved and adopted in full. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be the place identified in the Articles of Association within the People's Republic of China, and the Legal Representative is authorized to execute any lease, license, acceptance letter, landlord consent or service document necessary to establish and maintain the registered office and to file the same with the competent market supervision administration. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the authorized share capital of the Company is the amount stated in the Articles of Association, divided into such number of shares, of such class, voting rights, rights to profits and rights to surplus assets as stated therein; the share subscription by each shareholder is hereby ratified, adopted and confirmed; the Directors and officers are authorized to demand, deposit, receipt, hold, call and allocate all capital contributions in accordance with the contribution schedule, and no share is issued or deemed fully paid until the lawful consideration required in the Articles of Association has been actually received by the Company in money or in lawfully valued non-monetary property, and all provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China concerning subscribed capital and the five-year contribution period are complied with. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed to statutory offices of the Company: the executive director or board of directors as set out in the Articles, the legal representative, the supervisor, and the general manager, each holding office subject to the articles and for the term determined by law, with all powers and duties prescribed by the Company Law and the constitution of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that a basic deposit account, any capital verification account, and any foreign currency account of the Company shall be opened with a bank lawfully licensed in the People's Republic of China; the Legal Representative, General Manager, Chief Financial Officer or any two of them acting jointly are authorized to prepare, execute, endorse, deliver and attend to all account opening documents, specimen signature cards, bank mandates, online banking authorizations, wire transfer instructions, deposit slips, checks, drafts, promissory notes and other banking instruments; and the bank is authorized to act on such instructions until revoked in writing. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Directors and officers are directed to prepare, execute, sign, file and prosecute all registration applications, foreign investment information reports, tax registration and returns, social insurance registrations, statistical returns, public security seal registrations, and all licenses and permits including the insurance assessment business license, with the State Administration for Market Regulation, the State Taxation Administration, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the Ministry of Commerce or its reporting systems, the public security authorities and any other government office, and to pay all lawful fees and charges. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any act done prior to the date of these resolutions by any director, officer or agent of the Company in connection with the incorporation, registration, financing or licensing of the Company is hereby ratified, confirmed and adopted as an act of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability and Business Scope Pre-verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Registration Service Platform (SAMR); foreign investment access screening under the Negative List through the same platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name pre-registration application setting out at least three proposed English and Chinese company names, the limited liability company form, proposed ISIC-compatible business scope, registered capital, investment ratio and intended address. The platform screens for identical, confusingly similar or prohibited names and checks the proposed scope against the Foreign Investment Negative List. For a marine insurance surveyor WFOE, the business scope must be framed as marine cargo and hull insurance inspection, surveying, loss adjustment and claims assistance; if any item falls in the Negative List, a separate commerce authority approval path is required before registration. After approval, the name notice is generally valid for six months. The applicant should also confirm that the insurance assessment or surveying and loss adjustment language used in the business scope does not exceed the scope permitted for a WFOE without an NFRA license.
required_dossiers: Name pre-registration application form
Passport or corporate identity documents of all shareholders
Proposed business scope and registered capital schedule
Authorization letter of the filing applicant or agent
Draft Articles of Association if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or designated as unavailable, the applicant may file a new name application or an administrative review against an unlawful refusal; for a Negative List query, either remove the restricted item from the scope or apply for the required sectoral approval before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization and Capital Contribution Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chinese consulates and embassies or authorities competent to issue Apostille certificates in the shareholder's jurisdiction; local notary offices in China where instructed; the local SAMR office receives the finalized documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All corporate documents of foreign shareholders, including certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, parent board resolution, and powers of attorney, must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention or legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate where the Convention does not apply. Prepare bilingual Articles of Association, shareholder resolutions, capital contribution schedule and legal representative appointment. The company law no longer requires a paid-in minimum for ordinary WFOE, but all subscribed capital must be contributed within the five-year statutory cap; where capital is to be used for the NFRA-licensed surveyor operation, the shareholder should arrange the timing of contributions to match the license application and any regulator capital adequacy rules. A foreign exchange capital account can be opened after registration; no escrow or blocked capital account is imposed by company law.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or consular-legalized certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent
Certificate of good standing or equivalent
Parent board resolution approving incorporation and subscription
Notarized power of attorney appointing the filing representative
Draft Articles of Association in Chinese or bilingual
Capital contribution schedule and bank reference if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the documents are rejected for defective legalization, obtain a new Apostille from the designated authority in the jurisdiction of issue or re-submit through consular legalization; if the capital schedule is queried, revise it to comply with the five-year contribution period and submit a supplemental shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of WFOE Establishment Registration to SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or Provincial Administration for Market Regulation, business registration department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete establishment registration package through the SAMR online system or in person at the enterprise registration hall. The package includes the signed application form, the Articles of Association, proof of registered office, identity documents of the legal representative, executive director, supervisor and manager, the name approval notice, foreign investment information report and the legalized parent documents. SAMR examines the legality of the proposed company, the absence of a Negative List restriction, and the suitability of the legal representative. If accepted, SAMR issues the Business License for Enterprise as a Legal Person, records the WFOE in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, and shares the foreign investment information with the commerce authority. The WFOE is legally established on the date of license issuance.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Establishment Registration Application Form
Original name pre-approval notice
Signed Articles of Association
Proof of registered office, including lease agreement, property ownership certificate and landlord consent
Legalized identity and good-standing documents of shareholders
Identity certificates of directors, supervisor, legal representative and manager
Foreign Investment Information Report
Authorization and power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a correction request, correct the specified deficiencies within the period stated in the notice; if the matter is listed for inspection, respond with original documents and certified translations; if the application is rejected, apply for administrative reconsideration or re-file after curing the grounds of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seal Carving, Bank Account Opening, Tax and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving service; licensed commercial banks and banks handling SAFE foreign exchange registration; local office of the State Taxation Administration; local social insurance and housing fund authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, obtain the seal approval at the Public Security Bureau and arrange the company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, and invoice seal at a PSB-authorised engraving company. Open a basic deposit account and foreign currency or capital account at a licensed bank; complete the anti-money laundering and know-your-client procedures and beneficial ownership declaration, and obtain the bank account details. Register tax within thirty days on the electronic tax authority and apply for invoice and general taxpayer status as needed. Register social insurance, medical insurance and housing fund with the local authorities and report employees. Foreign exchange registration is completed through the bank under SAFE delegation; no separate SAFE registration certificate is issued for ordinary trade items, but the WFOE must submit foreign investment information annually.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Seal carving certificate
Legal representative identification
Articles of Association
Bank account opening application and KYC forms
Tax registration form and business scope
Social insurance and employee roster
Foreign investment information report receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an account opening is suspended for enhanced due diligence, provide an organizational chart, source of funds explanation, and proof of licensed activity; if tax registration is late, file an overdue registration and pay the prescribed late fee; for seal issues, reapply at the PSB-designated engraving office for replacement seals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Statutory Insurance Surveyor License (NFRA Operating Approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA) local office, Insurance Intermediary Supervision Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing marine insurance surveying operations, the WFOE must obtain the statutory insurance assessment institution license or equivalent surveyor and loss-adjustment operating permission under the Insurance Law. Submit the application to the local NFRA office or the one-stop acceptance point with the corporate license, articles, certified capital proof, professional indemnity insurance or financial responsibility arrangements, detailed business plan, management and compliance systems, procedures manual for hull and cargo surveys, claims documentation standards, and biographies and qualifications of surveyors and management. The NFRA will assess controlling shareholders fitness, professional indemnity protection, internal controls, business place, and the technical competence of survey staff. The company may not issue survey reports or charge premium-related fees before the license is granted; violation may lead to administrative penalties. The NFRA has to respond within the statutory time limit, and after approval, the company's business scope becomes operational for marine cargo and hull claims surveying.
required_dossiers: NFRA insurance assessment institution license application form
Original or certified copy of the WFOE business license and Articles of Association
Registered capital subscription and contribution certificate
Professional indemnity insurance certificate or guarantee arrangement
Surveyor and adjuster qualification certificates and employment contracts
Compliance, anti-fraud and claims handling manuals
Business plan and three-year financial projections
Legal representation authorization and identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NFRA issues a correction or supplementation notice, file the requested materials within the specified time and request an extension if translation is needed; if the application is returned as incomplete, re-submit after completing all statutory conditions; if denial is issued, apply for administrative reconsideration or bring an administrative lawsuit within the applicable legal limitation period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA) - Insurance Intermediary Supervision Department; no physical industrial licensing board applies to marine insurance surveying activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Insurance Assessment Institution Business License / Insurance Surveyor and Loss Adjuster Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment full Environmental Impact Assessment is not triggered for an office-based marine insurance surveyor with no manufacturing or physical installation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA report, environmental registration or environmental examination is required because the activity is a non-manufacturing marine consultancy and field inspection service
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no stationary emission sources, process wastewater, volatile organic compounds or hazardous waste streams are generated by the core surveying service; any port or vessel access is governed by maritime safety and port environmental rules requiring proper disposal of ship-generated waste and compliance with terminal operator safety instructions

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial civil defense fire permit; however, the ordinary commercial office must satisfy the Fire Protection Law through the appropriate fire safety acceptance or occupancy record, and the employer must comply with the Work Safety Law by providing office safety, port and vessel safety training, personal protective equipment, and any terminal-operator access permits required during hull and cargo surveys. No separate Civil Defense fire permit is required for marine insurance surveying services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); the electronic filing and registration portal is the national E-Tax Bureau (Electronic Tax Bureau) platform operated by the STA through provincial and municipal tax service bureaus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign investor must first complete name pre-registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). After SAMR approves the WFOE establishment, the business license is issued bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory taxpayer identification number for both Corporate Income Tax and VAT; SAMR data is automatically synchronized to the competent tax authority under the one-window service system. The WFOE must then complete tax initialization in the E-Tax Portal, including real-name verification of the legal representative, filing of the financial/accounting system and bank account, application for invoice types and quotas (including fully digitalized electronic invoices), and VAT general taxpayer qualification if required. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment that earns China-source income registers through the withholding agent at the competent district tax authority under the non-resident enterprise withholding registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity election. A WFOE is mandatorily an entity-level taxpayer under the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law; available elections such as VAT general versus small-scale taxpayer status do not alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China under the PRC VAT Law and implementing regulations; China's headline goods VAT rate is 13%, while marine insurance surveying qualifies as a taxed modern service normally subject to 6% VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 0 for mandatory basic tax registration of a newly incorporated WFOE (tax registration is due within 30 days of business license issuance); RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the mandatory threshold for VAT general taxpayer registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue invoices through the STA's fully digitalized electronic invoice system under the Golden Tax Phase IV framework. Invoice data are transmitted in real time to the STA's national VAT invoice service platform; each fully digitalized electronic invoice is assigned a unique electronic invoice number, and no physical fiscal stamp is required. Issuance, red-letter reversals, corrections, and voiding must be reported to the tax authority through the official e-invoice platform or an approved third-party API interface, and real-time fiscal clearance/anti-fraud digital matching is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under China's VAT export and cross-border service rules, exports of goods are zero-rated and eligible for export VAT refund, and eligible cross-border services supplied by a Chinese resident taxpayer to an overseas recipient for consumption wholly outside China may qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption under the VAT reform measures and subsequent STA announcements. Marine insurance claims surveying will qualify for zero-rating only if the service recipient is an overseas insurer/underwriter without a domestic establishment, the service is consumed and documented offshore, the subject risk, vessel, or cargo is not territorially taxable in China, and foreign-exchange receipts are received from outside China. A marine survey physically performed on Chinese territory for vessels or cargo located in China will generally be treated as a domestic taxable service subject to 6% VAT rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) / electronic customs export release notice issued by the General Administration of Customs of China
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, air waybill, or equivalent transport document proving physical export of goods (not applicable to service-only marine surveying)
Fully digitalized electronic invoice / commercial invoice describing the zero-rated export supply and overseas customer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / bank foreign-exchange receipt confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign counter-party

Signed cross-border service contract or underwriter mandate letter, claim file, survey report, vessel/cargo location evidence, and foreign customer status documentation demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA cross-matches export declarations, electronic invoice metadata, transport logistics documents, and foreign-exchange receipts with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. Failure to substantiate zero-rating within the required period results in reversal of the zero-rated claim and reassessment at the applicable domestic VAT rate (6% for services or 13% for goods), plus late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day and an administrative tax penalty between 50% and 500% of the underpaid tax. Fraudulently obtained export VAT refunds are clawed back in full and may attract a penalty of up to five times the refunded amount, with criminal liability potentially arising under PRC Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refund. Ordinary assessment periods generally run for three years, extended to ten years for major understatements, with no time limit in cases of fraud or non-payment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China maintains a bifurcated convertibility structure. RMB is fully convertible for current account transactions including trade in services, marine survey fees, insurance premiums, and routine operating disbursements, provided the underlying transaction is genuine, documented, and filed through the SAFE-monitored bank reporting system. Capital account items remain heavily regulated: foreign direct investment, cross-border financing, offshore guarantees, and any form of capital injection require either SAFE registration, bank-level Foreign Exchange (FX) registration, or PBOC approval. For a WFOE formed as a marine insurance surveyor, the initial paid-in capital must enter through a designated Foreign Investment Capital Settlement Account, be verified by a qualified capital verification report, and be used strictly within the approved business scope. Profit remittance to the foreign parent is a current account transaction, but it is practically gated by annual statutory audit completion, prior-year tax clearance, minutes of the shareholder distribution declaration, and the foreign exchange payment notice filed through the remitting bank; the bank will also screen for any outstanding SAFE sanctions or undisclosed related-party cross-border exposures. Surrender requirements are now largely repatriation-oriented rather than mandatory conversion: registered exporters and service providers must repatriate offshore foreign currency receipts through domestic banks, but may hold eligible current account receipts in foreign currency settlement accounts or convert to RMB at quoted spot rates. The practical hurdles for repatriating dividends are not convertibility itself but the evidential burden: banks demand audited financials, tax payment certificates, and contractual evidence of the underlying service income, and any mismatched invoice, contract, or tax return will stall the remittance for compliance review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished mandatory closed-period surrender of export proceeds. The legal rule is repatriation: all current account foreign exchange receipts arising from the marine surveying service contract must be brought into the entity's domestic foreign currency settlement account and cannot be retained offshore without SAFE approval. The converting entity may retain the foreign currency or sell it to a bank at the prevailing market rate; there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio. However, the bank must match each receipt to the underlying export/service transaction in the SAFE Trade Monitoring System, and any receipt unresolved against a contract or customs declaration beyond the standard monitoring window is flagged as a compliance exception.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI and full-service Foreign Currency Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account and Trade Service Foreign Currency Account
Capital Settlement Account and General Current Account
Operational RMB and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as a typical foreign fintech account provider or international wallet cannot lawfully domicile or service a Mainland-domiciled WFOE's primary treasury operations because they lack a PRC banking license and are not recognized as qualified settlement institutions under SAFE regulations. Such platforms are also barred from opening domestic CNY accounts or holding the entity's capital escrow balance. They may be used only as sub-ledger aids or for non-banking ancillary payment initiation, never as the primary regulated clearing rail. The bank account must sit with a licensed domestic commercial bank; Wise and similar services are not a substitute for corporate banking compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative and at least one statutory director must appear physically at the bank branch for the initial account opening and KYC interview. Remote notarization or consular proxy opening is not accepted for the initial corporate account establishment at Tier-1 commercial banks. If the legal representative is a non-resident, the bank may permit a duly authorized officer of the WFOE to attend after a notarized power of attorney is validated, but the bank retains the right to require the legal representative to attend a verification interview by video call or in a subsequent in-person visit before high-risk functions such as FX derivative authorization are activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity through a non-resident parent entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full corporate chain from the ultimate individual shareholders to the WFOE with notarized and apostilled certificates of incorporation, registered address proof, board resolutions authorizing the WFOE formation, clear organizational chart, passport copies of all senior beneficial owners, and a breakdown of share classes and voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and restricted shipping exposure within marine surveying receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an inventory of vessels, cargoes, insured entities, and counterparties screened against UN, EU, OFAC, and Chinese sanctions lists; include charter party or marine insurance policy excerpts, bills of lading where applicable, vessel IMO numbers, and a written internal policy confirming the surveyor will not service sanctioned cargo routes or flagged vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient evidence of genuine operating substance and statutory licensing for the surveying business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the WFOE business license reflecting the approved marine insurance survey and claims inspection scope, the statutory maritime surveyor license or qualification approval certificate, lease agreements for the China office, staff payroll, proposed equipment or survey tooling ownership, and the parent company's registered insurance intermediary or surveying credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncertain source of funds for the initial capital injection and future shareholder loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the foreign exchange registration form (FDI Basic Information), audited financial statements of the shareholder for the last two fiscal years, board resolution approving the capital amount, bank statements evidencing the source of the remitted funds, personal net worth documentation where natural person shareholders are involved, and a capital verification report to be issued by a PRC-certified accountant after the funds arrive.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection must arrive through an SWIFT or cross-border remittance into the FDI Capital Settlement Account at the chosen Tier-1 domestic bank after the company has obtained its business license, opened the bank account, and completed FX registration with SAFE through the bank. The payment must carry a clear purpose code describing foreign direct investment capital injection, and the remitter must match the registered shareholder exactly. The bank will verify the FDI declaration, monitor the actual payment against the registered capital amount, require a capital verification report in Chinese issued by a licensed PRC accounting firm, and then transfer eligible amounts into the RMB settlement account only after full review. Parent company loans must be separately registered as foreign debts if they exceed regulatory thresholds or maturities, and equity injections cannot be disguised as operating revenue.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating outflows such as surveyor subcontractor fees, reinsurance payments, and vessel equipment procurement, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 wire transfer with full remittance purpose codes and contract evidence held at the remitting bank. For large or documentary trade settlements involving vessel repairs, spare parts, or marine equipment, a Commercial Letter of Credit or Documentary Collection may be used, supported by commercial invoices, transport documents, and inspection certificates. All outbound disbursements must be matched to an underlying current account transaction; service payments require the signed survey contract, tax payment certificate for withholding if applicable, and a receipt from the foreign party. Capital account outflows, such as dividend remittances, require an additional distribution resolution, audited financials, tax clearance, and the SAFE-related remittance filing through the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instructions: Onshore CNY foreign exchange forwards and FX swaps with a real business background are permissible through licensed domestic banks.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not available onshore; only offshore entities may access NDF markets.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign debt are permissible after SAFE registration.
FX options and currency swaps are permitted only when hedging verified current account exposures or approved capital account liabilities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Market Entity Credit Report and integrated Foreign Investment Information Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, coordinated with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 30 June for the immediately preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing places the WFOE on the SAMR List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations and exposes it to a corrective order and a fine of up to RMB 10,000; if the abnormal status is not cured within three consecutive years, the WFOE is transferred to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, which is a statutory precondition for administrative revocation and strike-off of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Filing and Settlement (annual EIT reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the local tax service authority in the WFOE jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May each year for the prior tax year, which is on a calendar-year basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid tax after the deadline accrues a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the underpaid amount; the STA may additionally impose a fine of up to 50% of the underpaid tax and apply compulsory bank collection, asset seizure, and credit-control measures; persistent non-compliance may trigger an administrative find of unfitness and stronger tax collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements audit and certified audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent PRC-registered certified public accounting firm appointed by the shareholders or board, with the audited financial statements serving as the basis for SAMR annual report and tax settlement filings where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory audit must be completed before the 30 June SAMR annual report filing window and, in commercial practice, before the 31 May income tax settlement to support the tax filing; there is no separate government filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain the legally required audit constitutes a violation of the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law; directors and the legal representative may face personal liability, the annual report may be deemed inaccurate or incomplete, and the tax authority may reassess taxable income using adjusted or deemed methods with late-payment interest and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven registration change filing (shareholder, director, supervisor, registered address, paid-in capital, control or beneficial ownership changes), including annual beneficial ownership verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR for corporate registration changes and, for beneficial ownership information, the SAMR/People's Bank of China beneficial ownership information registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any qualifying change must be filed within 30 calendar days of the event during the year; the annual ownership and UBO verification is embedded in the 1 January to 30 June annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file changes within 30 days triggers a corrective order and administrative fines, generally up to RMB 10,000 or, in serious cases, RMB 20,000 to RMB 100,000; continued refusal to correct may lead to revocation of the business license, and false or incomplete beneficial ownership information may expose the entity to separate PBOC penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every limited-liability WFOE is legally required to appoint a licensed PRC certified public accounting firm to audit its annual financial statements for each fiscal year. The audit obligation is entity-form-based and not size-based: there is no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption applicable to a WFOE. Accordingly, the mandate applies regardless of total assets, annual revenue, or employee count; sectoral regulators for marine surveying and insurance-claims inspection may impose additional or more stringent audit and assurance requirements on the licensed WFOE.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC ASBE / China GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS; eligible small-scale entities may apply the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards, but a WFOE engaged in marine insurance-claims surveying and subject to foreign-investment reporting should prepare its statutory financial statements under full PRC ASBE. IFRS is not a substitute for PRC statutory reporting in China, although it may be used for parent-group consolidation and overseas purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain and confirm its true ultimate beneficial owners, including any individual holding 25% or more of equity, voting rights, or effective control, in the SAMR beneficial ownership information registration system; changes must be reported within 30 days of occurrence. The annual SAMR credit report also requires confirmation of the current shareholder and beneficial ownership structure. Any shareholding transfer or change in legal representative, directors, supervisors, registered address, or paid-in capital must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the event, and the confirmation made in the annual report must be consistent with the filed registers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders, equity interests, and paid-in capital records)
Register of Directors, Executive Officers, and Supervisors
Register of Charges, Pledges, and Encumbrances
Minute Book of shareholder and board meetings, including written resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,500 per annum in tier-1 Chinese cities, covering registered address provision, local administrative liaison, and registered agent or corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 8,000 per annum for a typical WFOE, increasing to USD 10,000 to USD 25,000 if the parent requires a group-level IFRS consolidation pack in addition to the PRC statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard PRC Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rate of 25%; qualified High and New Technology Enterprises pay 15%; Qualified Small Low-Profit Enterprises benefit from a reduced effective rate of approximately 5% on taxable income within applicable statutory thresholds (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million); R&D expenses enjoy an additional 100% deduction; Hainan Free Trade Port and certain encouraged industries may apply a 15% rate; no patent box or free-zone CIT holiday applies to an ordinary WFOE marine insurance surveyor.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A Class) Form A100000, together with Form A000000 Basic Information, deduction and adjustment schedules (including Form A105000), R&D super-deduction schedule, related-party transaction schedules, and, where applicable, the stand-alone Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return. Filing is completed online through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax/Electronic Tax Bureau) using the WFOE's Unified Social Credit Code and authorized digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement of CIT (annual reconciliation) with quarterly provisional CIT prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT prepayment returns are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The annual consolidated CIT return and final payment of tax are due within 5 months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e. by May 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Legal Identity and WFOE Registration Profile
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the WFOE's legal name, Unified Social Credit Code, registered address, legal form (wholly foreign-owned limited liability company), registered capital and paid-in capital structure, industry classification code (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390), principal business as marine claims inspection surveyor, date of incorporation, and details of the non-resident shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the non-resident investor's country of residence and assess DTA entitlement. Confirm the WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income. If the foreign investor conducts activities through the WFOE rather than through a branch, the WFOE itself is the taxable entity. Incorrect industry classification can trigger regulatory license review because marine insurance surveying is a licensed insurance ancillary activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Revenue and Total Accounting Profit Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter total accounting profit (total profit before tax) per PRC GAAP financial statements. Include all gross revenue from vessel hull and cargo damage marine claims inspections, survey reports, loss adjustment services, damage appraisals, expert testimony, and any fees remitted from overseas underwriters by wire, Wise, or equivalent payment rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Chinese-resident WFOE must include worldwide income. Fees received from a foreign underwriter or a non-resident related insurer are not automatically foreign-source income merely because the payment is remitted from abroad. No reduction is allowed for deemed offshore income unless a valid foreign tax credit schedule supports double tax relief on genuinely foreign-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-Taxable Income, Tax-Exempt Income, and Timing Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subtract qualifying non-taxable income and tax-exempt income from total accounting profit, including qualified treasury bond interest, certain restricted-use government grants meeting statutory conditions, and dividend income received from a Chinese resident company if all requirements are satisfied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not exclude dividends received from a non-resident parent or an offshore intermediate holding company unless proper foreign tax credit treatment is claimed. Treaty exemptions do not create CIT tax-exempt income in the annual return unless the schedule has a specific legal basis. Any government grant received to support marine surveying operations should be examined under CIT-implementation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Deduction Adjustment, Expense Disallowances, and Special Limits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply statutory deduction limitations and add-backs: business entertainment is deductible at 60% of qualifying expenditure but capped at 0.5% of net revenue; advertising and promotion expenses generally capped at 15% of revenue; staff benefit and welfare expenses, union expenditures, and education funds are subject to payroll caps; charitable donations are capped at 12% of annual accounting profit; expenses lacking valid tax invoices must be added back; intercompany service fees must be arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments by the WFOE to non-resident group companies for management services, survey methodology, quality assurance, IT systems, brand royalties, or technical support are closely scrutinized. Each payment must be supported by a contract, invoice, proof of actual service performed, demonstrative benefit to the WFOE, and arm's-length benchmarking. If the payment is characterized as a royalty or interest, separate withholding tax obligations arise; if the non-resident provider is treated as having a Chinese permanent establishment through the WFOE, a 25% CIT assessment may apply instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Loss Carryforward and Taxable Income Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset prior-year CIT-recognized tax losses within the statutory five-year forward period and compute net taxable income for the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the WFOE's own China-recognized losses may be deducted. Losses of the foreign parent, non-resident subsidiaries, or overseas branches generally cannot offset the WFOE's Chinese taxable income unless specific CIT provisions permit consolidated foreign loss treatment with adequate evidentiary support. Loss carryforward documentation must be preserved for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Rate, Tentative Tax Liability, Credits, and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the applicable CIT rate (25% standard or 15% if the WFOE qualifies as a High and New Technology Enterprise, or the effective preferential regime for Qualified Small Low-Profit Enterprises if eligible), compute tentative CIT payable, deduct quarterly prepayments already made, apply foreign tax credits only within the statutory cap, and determine final self-assessment payable or refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Profit distributions to non-resident shareholders are not deductible at the WFOE level. There is no deemed-paid foreign tax credit on dividends flowing from the WFOE to its overseas parent. If the WFOE has foreign-source income derived through a foreign branch, the foreign tax credit is limited by the PRC tax attributable to that foreign-source income. Any final tax payment must be made by the May 31 deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach related-party transaction schedules disclosing all connected transactions with the non-resident shareholder, parent group, sister entities, and key management: marine survey services, management fees, intercompany loans, interest, royalties, lease payments, asset transfers, and capital transactions. State whether contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File, Master File, or Country-by-Country Report) is required and maintained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party pricing must satisfy the arm's-length principle under PRC CIT Law. For a marine insurance surveyor, typical comparables include independent survey and inspection service providers. The WFOE must show sufficient employees, premises, marine survey equipment, insurance certificates, and risk-bearing capacity to justify the profit it retains. A residual profit split is not available to shift profits offshore where the WFOE performs the core income-generating activities. Incomplete disclosures may lead to deemed income re-determination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Non-Resident Enterprise Withholding and Profit Repatriation Schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Although not a line on Form A100000, the WFOE must file a separate Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return when paying dividends, interest, royalties, or rent to a foreign shareholder or non-resident beneficiary. The withholding return calculates gross amount, statutory or treaty rate, and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting any dividend to the non-resident parent, the WFOE must confirm that final CIT settlement has been completed, adequate distributable profits exist, and the required withholding tax is paid. For an ordinary corporate non-resident recipient, the statutory dividend WHT is 10%; treaty relief may apply only if the parent provides a valid Tax Residency Certificate and establishes beneficial ownership and substantive economic activity. Under-withholding and remittance of dividend without withholding creates immediate director and officer exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual CIT return by May 31 triggers late-filing penalties under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law: statutory fine up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious circumstances. Unpaid or underpaid tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% under Article 32. Tax evasion through false declarations, hidden revenue, fake invoices, or fictitious deductions is penalized under Articles 63 and 64: recovery of underpaid tax, daily surcharge, and an administrative penalty from 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. Withholding agents that fail to withhold and remit may be penalized from 50% to 300% of the unremitted withheld tax under Article 69. Criminal tax fraud is punishable under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law with imprisonment up to three years in ordinary cases and three to seven years for large evasion amounts; tax authorities may also apply exit-control measures and travel bans under Article 44 of the Tax Collection Administration Law for individuals with outstanding tax liabilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid by the Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise; 20% is the statutory rate on dividends paid to a non-resident individual shareholder; DTA relief commonly reduces the corporate dividend WHT to 5% for a beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the WFOE's shares and to 10% in most other cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the WFOE, as withholding agent, must receive and retain before payment: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the shareholder's residence country for the year in which the income is paid; (2) a duly executed beneficial ownership self-certification and, where required, treaty benefit claim forms accepted by the Chinese tax authority; (3) evidence that the non-resident recipient is the beneficial owner and not a conduit or shell, including actual business operations, hiring of substantive personnel, office premises in the residence jurisdiction, and real control and use of the income; (4) sufficient documentation that the dividends are declared out of after-CIT distributable profits; and (5) where withholding already occurred at the statutory rate, a refund application may be filed with the Chinese tax authority within three years under the Tax Collection Administration Law if the treaty condition is satisfied retrospectively. Treaty relief is denied if the arrangement has no bona fide commercial substance and exists merely to obtain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on China-source royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% of the gross amount under the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law. DTA rates vary by treaty and type of income; commonly negotiated royalty and interest rates range from 5% to 10%, with particular treaty provisions for equipment royalties, know-how, bank interest, and finance lease charges. If the non-resident recipient has a Chinese permanent establishment to which the royalty or interest is effectively connected, the 10% WHT does not apply and the income is instead subject to regular CIT at 25% with the recipient filing or settling through the PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the PRC special tax adjustment documentation rules (SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42), a Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions reach: RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers or license/use arrangements; RMB 100 million for financial asset transactions; or RMB 40 million for provision of services. A Master File may be required when prior-year related-party revenue reaches the applicable high threshold, and Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least RMB 5.5 billion in the preceding fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime; however, the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, together with the beneficial ownership test in SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9, impose substance-over-form and economic substance requirements. A WFOE marine insurance surveyor must perform its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in China: employing qualified marine surveyors and inspectors, maintaining local office and inspection equipment, making key commercial decisions in China, assuming genuine professional liability and operating risk, and deriving its performance-based service revenue from actual economic functions. If the WFOE claims treaty benefits, distributes profits, or charges intercompany fees while having little or no economic substance, the tax authority may deny treaty benefits, recharacterize the transaction, deem taxable income, and pierce the corporate veil where shareholders abuse limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately omits survey fees received from overseas underwriters through wire or Wise, issues false marine survey invoices, creates fictitious deductible costs through shell vendors, underreports taxable income, or destroys business records for the purpose of evading CIT and related taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Articles 32, 63, and 64, the tax authority will recover the underpaid tax, impose daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and levy an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax. If the amount of tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the tax due, PRC Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal liability: up to three years imprisonment or detention and a fine; for huge amounts and more than 30% of the tax due, three to seven years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, actual controllers, and chief financial officers who knowingly approve or participate in false accounting cannot hide behind corporate limited liability. Under the PRC Company Law veil-piercing doctrine, a shareholder that abuses the separate legal personality of the WFOE or co-mingles corporate and personal assets is jointly and severally liable for creditors' losses. Responsible individuals may be subject to exit-control measures, travel bans, property freezing, and asset restitution. Criminal conviction for tax evasion carries direct imprisonment, fines, and prohibition from serving as company director or manager.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE performs all core marine survey operations in China but charges the non-resident parent or related underwriter a deliberately low service fee so that the WFOE reports low or negative profit, fails to maintain contemporaneous Local File documentation, pays excessive management fees or royalties to an offshore shell, and omits related-party disclosures from the CIT schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority is empowered under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41, 44, and 48 to make special tax adjustments, adjust taxable income according to arm's-length comparables, and assess additional tax and interest on the underpaid tax. Failure to provide related-party transaction documentation allows deemed income assessment and may also trigger penalties under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 where the substance of the arrangement amounts to fraudulent underpayment. Similarly structured transactions may be denied deduction, and the interest charged may include a benchmark loan interest rate plus a punitive uplift of five percentage points under the special tax adjustment regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and chief officers who sign false transfer pricing documentation or approve artificial service fee structures face personal civil liability if the WFOE becomes insolvent as a result of excessive profit drains. The courts may pierce the corporate veil where the arrangement is used to divert corporate assets for private benefit or to evade taxes. Officers may be blacklisted by the tax authority and prevented from leaving China while tax adjustments are outstanding; in egregious cases, criminal fraud and evasion charges may extend to the individuals who approved the TP scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Repatriation Withholding Non-Compliance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends to an offshore intermediate holding company in Hong Kong or Singapore while the recipient has no employees, no physical office, no real economic activity, and no substance other than holding shares; the WFOE then claims a reduced 5% DTA withholding rate without obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership evidence, fails to withhold the statutory 10% corporate income tax before remitting funds, and wires dividends out of China through payment rails without filing the withholding return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 37 and 40 and Tax Collection Administration Law Article 69, the withholding agent must withhold and remit the tax on the gross dividend; failure to do so exposes the WFOE to a penalty of 50% to 300% of the unremitted withheld tax, recovery of the unpaid tax, and daily late-payment surcharge. A treaty claim will be denied if the recipient is found to be a conduit lacking beneficial ownership, meaning the full statutory 10% WHT and penalties apply. Under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the transaction may be recharacterized and the tax benefit disallowed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers who authorize dividend payments without ensuring withholding remittance are personally exposed to penalties and possible criminal liability if the non-remittance constitutes fraud or misappropriation. The tax authority may impose travel bans on representatives of the WFOE until outstanding withholding tax is settled. If the shareholder or director has used the WFOE as a mere instrument to extract profits and evade creditor or tax claims, the corporate veil may be pierced and the shareholder may be held personally liable for the unpaid withholding taxes, penalties, and interest.
